title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 7
paragraphs: The Lacedaemonians, in fact, were keeping a festival during this time and celebrating the Hyakinthia; they counted it of the utmost importance to attend to the things concerning the god, while at the same time the wall they had been building at the Isthmus was at this very moment being completed with battlements. And when the envoys from the Athenians came to Lacedaemon — bringing with them also envoys from Megara and Plataea — they came before the Ephors and said as follows: “The Athenians sent us to say that the king of the Medes not only offers to give us back our land, but also wishes to make us his allies on fair and equal terms without deceit or treachery, and is even willing to give us another land in addition to our own, whichever we choose. We, however, out of respect for Zeus of the Greeks and disdaining to be traitors to Greece, did not agree but refused — although we were unjustly treated by the other Greeks and left to destruction, and although we knew it was more profitable to make a treaty with the Persian than to carry on the war. Nor shall we make a treaty at any future time, if we have our way. Thus sincerely is our duty done toward the Greeks. But as for you, after having come into great dread lest we should make a treaty with the Persian, as soon as you learned for certain what our spirit was — that we would never betray Greece — and because your wall across the Isthmus is all but finished, you now make no account of the Athenians; though you agreed with us to come into Boeotia to meet the Persian, you have now deserted us, and you permitted the barbarian to invade Attica. For the present, then, the Athenians are angry with you, for you did not do what was right. They now bid you with all speed to send out an army with us, so that we may receive the barbarian in the land of Attica; for since we have missed Boeotia, the most suitable place to fight in our land is the Thriasian plain.”
